newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan finance minister reveals political donations.
newsitem.headline: Japan finance minister reveals political donations.

text.p: Japan's new Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday that a political faction which he heads received donations from an oil trader at the centre of a tax evasion scandal.
But Mitsuzuka, who was named finance minister in Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's government when it was formed last week, said the donations were legal and proper and did not constitute a bribe.

Mitsuzuka said his faction, the second biggest in the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), received a total of 6.5 million yen ($58,500) from millionaire oil wholesaler Junichi Izui over a two-year period starting in 1992.
"We were not asked to do anything (in return for Izui's political donations)," he told a regular news conference. "It was not a donation of that sort."
The 60-year-old Izui, owner and sole employee of oil wholesaler Izui Oil Co, was arrested last Thursday on suspicion of evading 310 million yen ($2.79 million) in taxes.

With Japanese newspapers reporting that Izui made donations to some of the nation's key politicians, his tax evasion case has taken on political overtones and has proved an embarrassment for Hashimoto's new minority government. ($1=111 yen)
